semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Geographical ecology is a subset of ecology that focuses on the spatial aspects of ecological phenomena. Therefore, while they are not exactly equivalent, they are considered semantically equivalent in the context of focusing on ecological concerns.

parent_domains.justification: Geographical ecology is a subset of the broader field of ecology, emphasizing spatial patterns and processes.
This domain combines aspects of ecological study with environmental aspects, inherently encompassing geographical ecology.
This domain links both ecological and environmental sciences, forming a broader perspective that includes geographical concepts.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Geographical ecology is most closely related to the general study of ecology, as it directly deals with ecological processes in a geographical context.

child_domains.justification: This domain specifically focuses on the distribution of species across different geographical areas, aligning closely with geographical ecology.

closest_child_domain.justification: Species distribution modeling is a specialized field that intersects significantly with geographical ecology by addressing the geographical distribution aspect of species.

sibling_domains.justification: Similar to geographical ecology, ecological modeling focuses on representing ecological phenomena, although not specifically bound to geographical aspects.
This domain similarly deals with measuring and analyzing ecological data, which can be applicable to geographical studies.
While focusing more on behavior, it still deals with ecological interactions that may be geographically relevant.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Ecological modeling shares the most similarity with geographical ecology because it involves constructing models to simulate ecological processes, which can include geographical components.
